reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Since August 2026, CRM dispute-ticket volume has roughly doubled (610→1260/month) primarily because a majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) carry an ACTUAL meter read that was accepted into billing despite being erroneous, with billing import/validation currently treating ACTUAL reads as trusted and not catching this error (E-04). A smaller share of disputes stems from estimate substitution tied to a manual-read route completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, E-01). The surge is not attributable to slow ticket response (within SLA, E-02) or a tariff change (none logged, E-05).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Since August 2026, CRM dispute-ticket volume roughly doubled (610→1260/month, E-03). The dominant confirmed mechanism: billing import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling 'none' (E-14), while firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report in 0.1 m3 units (E-13); valid v4.2 reads therefore appear ~10x inflated and are rejected REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, forcing estimate substitution that accounts for 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills (95.5%, E-12). This is a billing-config defect, not an AMI/MDMS pipeline failure (H-AMI-MDMS-PIPELINE-FAILURE rejected by E-14) nor field staffing/route lateness (rejected by E-12). The mechanism behind the separate majority of disputed bills carrying an ACTUAL read type (1785 of 3025, E-04) remains unestablished by current evidence.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
